text:
Chandler Stephenson has two Stanley Cup rings and 13 points in 20 games, 11 of them assists, 6 on the power play. Read only the box score and he looks like the playmaking center Seattle signed. The underlying numbers tell a harder story.

At 5v5, the Kraken get 38% of the shot attempts and 38% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than 10 points worse than when he sits. He has 16 shots in 20 games, and his own chances are thin. He's pointless in his last four, and the chances have thinned out too.

There is a counterweight. Seattle has scored 6.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, and that kind of gap usually swings back, which could add points without the play changing. Evolving-Hockey's read from last season cuts both ways: he plays with weaker teammates (bottom 4%), which drags down his raw numbers, but opponents also got 0.39 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, bottom 1% of forwards. At 32, the question is whether his minutes, 17:34 a night, hold if the play doesn't turn.
headline: Stephenson's assists hide a hard season
